explanations.explanation: It appears that this feature fires strongly on text that is highly structured and technical—segments laden with specialized, formal notation (such as mathematical formulas, scientific expressions, or code) and non‐standard punctuation or formatting typical of academic and technical discourse.

It appears that this feature “lights‐up” on text that isn’t ordinary flowing prose but instead is written in a meta or “stage‐direction” style—that is, it picks out passages that serve as extratextual or paratextual signals. In many high‐activation examples the language isn’t delivering content in a traditional narrative way but is instead formatted as sound effects (“DRUMROLL”, “WATER SOUND”), interjections, usernames, timestamps, filenames or other structured markers (including onomatopoeia, all‐caps labels and “dialogue” identifiers). In short, the feature seems to represent a signal for text that functions as non–canonical, metadata– or script–style commentary rather than standard narrative content.

It appears that this feature “lights up” when the text switches into a highly structured, technical register—one in which tokens belong to formal, metadata‐style formats (such as dates, file paths, code snippets, command‐line messages, mathematical formulas, and technical nomenclature). In short, the neuron is sensitive to passages that use specialized, structured language and formatting to convey technical or domain‐specific information.
